server.name: nyc-charter-laws-rules
server.title: NYC Charter, Administrative Code and Rules MCP server
server.description: An MCP server for searching and reading the New York City Charter, the Administrative Code and the Rules of the City of New York. It answers from an index BetaNYC builds from American Legal Publishing's bulk XML downloads, which ships with the package. It is for research only, not legal advice, and not the official text: check the code library before relying on any section.
keywords: rules of the city of new york

sources.title: New York City Charter
sources.what: The text of the New York City Charter, one record per section or chapter heading, with its citation and heading.
sources.source_name: New York City Charter, bulk XML download
sources.how_gathered: BetaNYC downloads the bulk XML file from American Legal Publishing's New York City code library, the site the NYC Law Department contracted for the Charter, Administrative Code and Rules, and builds an index from it. A scheduled job refreshes the index daily and publishes a new release when the text changed. The index ships with the npm package, so this server answers without going online.

changes.detail: The XML is split into one record per section or heading, with its citation pulled from the heading. BetaNYC also fixes text problems from the conversion: it decodes character codes the XML left as text (such as non-breaking spaces), removes American Legal Publishing's editing markers (such as [ALP S-054]) that leak into the body text, and puts back the space between a list number and the words after it. Deeper structure, such as which sections sit inside which title, is not kept.

known_gaps: Only the current text: no earlier versions of a section.
The index is flat, so get_title returns chapter and title headings, not every section inside them.
An XML file that cannot be read during the build is skipped, with a warning in the build log.

terms.credit_line: Source: New York City Charter, American Legal Publishing code library for the City of New York.

caveats: Not legal advice. American Legal Publishing says its codes may not yet reflect the most current legislation, and may have temporary errors or omissions.
How current the text is: get_version gives the publisher's own 'current through' line. The date about_data reports is when BetaNYC built this server's index from the download.
The publisher also takes error reports by phone, 800-445-5588, and the NYC Law Department takes them at NYCCodeRulesCharter@law.nyc.gov.
